newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam slows foreign investment approvals.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam slows foreign investment approvals.

text.p: Foreign investment in Vietnam, considered essential for the country's economic lift-off, fell sharply in the first nine months of 1996 due to a slowdown in the rate of project approvals, state media said on Monday.
Vietnam News Agency said 222 projects worth $3.96 billion were licensed between January and the end of September.
Official data was not available but according to a Reuters tally projects worth at least $5.47 billion were approved during the corresponding period in 1995.
The VNA report gave no reason for the slower approval rate but said a further 140 projects with proposed investment of about $6.2 billion were under consideration.
Hanoi has been sensitive to reports in recent months that foreign investment interest may be tapering off.
Officials said enthusiasm among investors remained high and the slowdown reflected only a determination on Hanoi's part to focus on the quality rather than the quantity of projects.
The VNA report said Asian investors from Taiwan, South Korea and Singapore were leading the pack this year with approved projects collectively worth $1.627 billion since January.
Foreign businesses have pledged a total of around $22 billion towards projects in Vietnam since economic and social reforms in the late 1980s, but only a fraction of this has been disbursed.
